### Root Cause

During book release (`Book.finalize_release`), two separate in-memory `Book` instances were loaded for the same database row before the transaction began:
1. `book = find(id)` loaded one `Book` instance.
2. `marker = ReleaseMarker.for(id)` loaded a second `Book` instance (`@book`) via `Book.drafts.find_by(id: book_id)` while `@book.title` still held the working title.

Inside the transaction, `book.update!(title: ..., subtitle: ...)` updated the title in the database on the first instance, and then `marker.publish!` called `@book.update!(published: true)` on the second instance, which still held the stale working title in memory (while ActiveRecord's partial update preserved the new title in the database). When the transaction committed, ActiveRecord deduplicated `after_update_commit` callbacks across instances of the same record and ran `Book::Recap#write_recap` on the last saved instance (`marker`'s `@book`), caching `{ title: <working title>, published: true }` until the book was saved again or the recap expired.

### Solution

- **`app/models/release_marker.rb`**: Reload `@book` (when persisted) in `ReleaseMarker#publish!` before setting `published: true` so it picks up any updates already made earlier in the transaction.
- **`app/models/book/recap.rb`**: Fetch the committed `:title` and `:published` attributes from the database in `write_recap` (`Book.where(id: id).pick(:title, :published)`) before writing to `Rails.cache`, while preserving per-book cache keys (`[ "book_recap", id ]`) and the configured expiration schedule (`Rails.application.config.x.recap.expires_in`).
- **Tests**: Added unit and integration tests in `test/models/book/recap_test.rb` and `test/controllers/books/releases_controller_test.rb` covering book releases, ordinary renames, multi-instance transactions, per-book recap isolation, and configured expiration.
